title: Probe exceptions and outliers during requirements interviews
goal: Help the requirements interview skill consistently notice exception cases and ask targeted follow-up questions when they affect product requirements.
in_scope: Update the project-local requirements-interview skill to consider exceptions, boundaries, and outlier scenarios while interpreting each meaningful user answer.
Treat absolute or broad wording such as all, always, never, and must as a prompt to check the rule's population, applicability conditions, and exceptions.
Provide adaptable exception lenses such as entity or actor states, availability or eligibility, timing, resource conflicts, missing or invalid information, and failure or recovery paths.
Ask concise follow-up questions only when an exception or outlier could materially change the requirement, workflow, scope, or expected behavior.
Record confirmed exception behavior and unresolved cases without inventing a policy or treating a hypothetical as a user decision.
out_of_scope: Enumerating every imaginable edge case for every answer.
Changing the harness CLI or automatically deciding business policies.
acceptance_criteria: The skill instructs the agent to consider relevant exceptions and outliers for each meaningful answer throughout the interview.
Absolute wording such as all, always, never, or must triggers a check of who or what is covered and when the rule may not apply.
The skill gives useful but non-exhaustive lenses for generating domain-relevant edge-case candidates.
The agent asks targeted follow-ups when different answers would materially change requirements, and avoids burdening the user with irrelevant hypotheticals.
The agent records confirmed exception rules separately from assumptions and unresolved cases, without inventing policy.
